taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM ET (Eastern Time) on September 30, 2026 to Madrid local time (CEST - Central European Summer Time in late September).

In late September 2026:
- ET (Eastern Time) would be EDT (Eastern Daylight Time), which is UTC-4
- Madrid would be in CEST (Central European Summer Time), which is UTC+2

The time difference is 6 hours (Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET).

5:00 PM ET = 17:00 ET
17:00 + 6 hours = 23:00 (11:00 PM)

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time Zone (PET), which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru does not observe daylight saving time).

To convert July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC to Lima time:
- Subtract 5 hours from UTC
- 12:00 - 5:00 = 07:00

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Timezone Conversion

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2.
Tokyo is in JST (Japan Standard Time), which is UTC+9.

The difference is 7 hours ahead for Tokyo.

June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST = June 1, 2026 at 4:00 PM JST

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Converting PDT to Madrid Time

PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) is UTC-7
Madrid is in CEST (Central European Summer Time) during October, which is UTC+2

The time difference is: UTC+2 minus UTC-7 = 9 hours ahead

October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT:
- Add 9 hours
- 11:59 PM + 9 hours = 8:59 AM the next day

Therefore, the deadline in Madrid time is October 12, 2026 at 8:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Time Zone Conversion

Madrid operates on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) or Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) depending on daylight saving.

In March 2026, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1), as daylight saving in Europe begins on March 29, 2026.

PST (Pacific Standard Time) is UTC-8.

The deadline is March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST.

Time difference: CET is 9 hours ahead of PST.

11:59 PM PST on March 3 = 11:59 + 9 hours = 8:59 AM CET on March 4

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 10:00 AM CET on February 2, 2026 to Los Angeles time.

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1.
Los Angeles is in PST (Pacific Standard Time) during February, which is UTC-8.

The time difference is: UTC+1 minus UTC-8 = 9 hours ahead.
So CET is 9 hours ahead of PST.

If the deadline is 10:00 AM CET on February 2, I subtract 9 hours:
10:00 AM - 9 hours = 1:00 AM PST on February 2.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Time Zone Conversion

Let me work through this step by step:

**Given deadline:** 8:00 AM JST (Japan Standard Time) on May 5, 2026

**Time zone offsets from UTC:**
- JST (Japan Standard Time): UTC+9
- PET (Peru Standard Time): UTC-5

**Difference:** JST is 14 hours ahead of PET

**Calculation:**
8:00 AM JST May 5 minus 14 hours = 6:00 PM PET May 4

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 11:59 PM PT on October 28, 2026 to Madrid time (CET/CEST).

PT (Pacific Time) is UTC-7 in October 2026 (PDT - daylight saving time is still in effect).
Madrid observes CET/CEST, which is UTC+1 in October 2026 (CEST - daylight saving time is still in effect).

The time difference is: UTC+1 minus UTC-7 = 8 hours ahead.

So 11:59 PM PT on October 28 = 11:59 on October 28 + 8 hours = 7:59 AM on October 29 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 9:00 AM ET (Eastern Time) on October 30, 2026 to Madrid local time.

Madrid is in Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1 in winter. In October, Spain observes CET (daylight saving time ends on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026).

Eastern Time in October is EDT (Eastern Daylight Time), which is UTC-4.

The time difference between EDT and CET is:
UTC+1 - (UTC-4) = 5 hours ahead

So 9:00 AM EDT = 9:00 AM + 5 hours = 2:00 PM CET

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Time Zone Conversion

You're in New York, which observes Eastern Time. In late October, New York is on **EDT (Eastern Daylight Time)**, which is **UTC-4**.

CET (Central European Time) is **UTC+1**.

**Time difference:** CET is 5 hours ahead of EDT.

**Conversion:**
- October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET
- Subtract 5 hours: 18:00 - 5:00 = 13:00 EDT

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 11:59 PM PT on November 2, 2026 to Madrid local time.

Madrid is in Central European Time (CET) or Central European Summer Time (CEST) depending on the season.

In November 2026, Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1), as daylight saving time ends in late October.

PT (Pacific Time) in early November is PDT (UTC-7), as daylight saving time doesn't end until early November in the US.

Time difference: CET is UTC+1, PDT is UTC-7, so Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PT.

November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT = November 3, 2026 at 7:59 AM CET

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Deadline Conversion

You're in Madrid, Spain (Central European Time - CET/CEST).

The deadline is March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time).

**Time difference calculation:**
- Pacific Time in March 2026 will be PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), UTC-7
- Madrid in March 2026 will be CET (Central European Time), UTC+1
- Difference: 8 hours ahead

**Conversion:**
- 11:59 PM PT on March 20 = 23:59 on March 20
- Add 8 hours = 07:59 on March 21

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 12:00 PM CET on March 25, 2026 to Los Angeles time.

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1.
Los Angeles is in Pacific Time, which in March would be PDT (Pacific Daylight Time) at UTC-7.

The time difference is: UTC+1 to UTC-7 = 8 hours behind.

So 12:00 PM (noon) CET minus 8 hours = 4:00 AM PDT.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

# Deadline Conversion to Madrid Time

Let me work through this:

1. **The deadline**: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026
   - 12:00 AM ET = midnight at the start of October 12
   - This is 00:00 ET on October 12, 2026

2. **Time zone difference**: 
   - ET (Eastern Time) in October 2026 will be EDT (Eastern Daylight Time, UTC-4)
   - Madrid is in CEST (Central European Summer Time, UTC+2) in October
   - Difference: Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET

3. **Conversion**:
   - 00:00 ET on October 12 + 6 hours = 06:00 CEST on October 12

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert October 9, 2026 at 23:59 AoE (Anywhere on Earth) to Madrid local time.

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is based on UTC-12, which is the last timezone on Earth to reach a given date. So October 9, 2026 at 23:59 AoE means the deadline is at October 10, 2026 at 11:59 UTC (adding 12 hours).

Madrid is in the CEST (Central European Summer Time, UTC+2) timezone in October 2026, since daylight saving time is still in effect.

Converting October 10, 2026 at 11:59 UTC to CEST:
11:59 UTC + 2 hours = 13:59 CEST

So the deadline in Madrid local time is October 10, 2026 at 13:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 12:00 PM PT (Pacific Time) on August 14, 2026 to Madrid local time (CEST - Central European Summer Time in August).

PT in August is PDT (UTC-7)
Madrid in August is CEST (UTC+2)

The time difference is 9 hours ahead for Madrid.

12:00 PM PDT = 12:00 PT on August 14
Add 9 hours: 12:00 + 9:00 = 21:00 (9:00 PM)

So the deadline in Madrid time is 21:00 on August 14, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 11:59 PM IST (Indian Standard Time) on November 10, 2026 to Madrid local time (CET/CEST).

IST is UTC+5:30
Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) in winter or CEST (UTC+2) in summer

In November, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1), as daylight saving time ends in late October.

11:59 PM IST on November 10 = 23:59 IST on November 10

Converting from IST to UTC:
23:59 IST = 23:59 - 5:30 = 18:29 UTC on November 10

Converting from UTC to CET (UTC+1):
18:29 UTC = 18:29 + 1:00 = 19:29 CET on November 10

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026 to Lima, Peru time.

First, let me identify the time zones:
- Nepal Standard Time (NST): UTC+5:45
- Lima, Peru: Peru Standard Time (PET): UTC-5

The time difference between Nepal and Lima:
5:45 - (-5) = 10:45 hours ahead

So Nepal is 10 hours and 45 minutes ahead of Lima.

If the deadline is 5:00 PM (17:00) on April 2, 2026 in Nepal time, I need to subtract 10 hours and 45 minutes:

17:00 on April 2 minus 10:45 = 6:15 on April 2

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 10:00 AM Adelaide time on October 6, 2026 to Madrid time.

Adelaide is in Australian Central Standard Time (ACST), which is UTC+9:30.
Madrid is in Central European Time, which is either CET (UTC+1) in winter or CEST (UTC+2) in summer.

In October, Madrid observes Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2.

Time difference: Adelaide (UTC+9:30) is 7 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Madrid (UTC+2).

So 10:00 AM in Adelaide = 10:00 - 7:30 = 2:30 AM in Madrid on the same day (October 6).

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 02:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to convert 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026 to Madrid time.

**Key information:**
- Sydney is in AEDT (Australian Eastern Daylight Time) in October, which is UTC+11
- Madrid is in CEST (Central European Summer Time) in October, which is UTC+2

**Calculation:**
- 6:00 PM (18:00) Sydney time on October 3, 2026 = October 3, 18:00 AEDT
- Convert to UTC: 18:00 - 11 hours = October 3, 07:00 UTC
- Convert to Madrid time: 07:00 + 2 hours = October 3, 09:00 CEST

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 09:00
